actions: Verified the full-rerun disruption counts and all six repair-rate rows directly from the current arXiv primary paper for SymTrace/SymFail.
Verified the paper's explicit causal limitation that Suspicious-Node jointly changes symptom-based target selection and repair guidance.

Verified ToolMisuseBench aggregate and fault-specific public-test rows from its primary paper, including zero success on released authorization/rate-limit subsets and the lightweight-policy limitation.

Verified the linked official ToolMisuseBench repository currently exposes deterministic generation/evaluation and reproduce-paper surfaces, without claiming an independent local rerun of the table values.
material_findings: Full rerun has a large observed success-to-failure disruption channel in the specific SymTrace setting: 85/162 reruns failed and 39/54 initially successful source cases regressed at least once.

Suspicious-Node's 20.15% pass@1 exceeds all task-level pass@3 baselines, but its target selector and symptom-conditioned guidance are a bundled intervention rather than separately identified causal components.

ToolMisuseBench confirms strong fault-class dependence: schema/timeout recovery improves under simple repair while released authorization/rate-limit subsets remain at zero measured success; this is not evidence that stronger replanning cannot recover those classes.
Aggregate success stayed 0.250 for all three released ToolMisuseBench baselines despite fault-local recovery differences, so aggregate success can hide recovery mechanism changes in this profile.
exact_next_action: Rotate to sealed C24 failure_evidence; prioritize a primary artifact that can separate measured failure from mechanism attribution or materially change downstream evidence status.
